blocks.text: One-sentence argument

Replacing an even tetramer by an odd pentamer reorganizes the low-energy sector of the Heisenberg cluster chain: the positive-coupling pentamer retains an effective spin-1/2 doublet with antiferromagnetic inter-cell exchange, weak virtual-process-induced frustration and momentum-selective local excitations, whereas any additional phases in the negative-alpha sector must be decided by the ongoing finite-size, multi-diagnostic campaign rather than inherited from the tetramer phase diagram.
Provisional title
Odd-cell spin-1/2 physics and momentum-selective excitations in a pentamer Heisenberg chain
Abstract · working version

Clustered quantum magnets provide a setting in which unit-cell parity can reorganize the low-energy degrees of freedom. Complete isolated-cell diagonalization gives an even-parity S=1/2 ground-state doublet for alpha>0, an S=3/2 ground multiplet for alpha<0, and a degeneracy at alpha=0. Projecting the positive-side doublet yields J_eff/beta=0.4189–0.4396 at representative points, while second-order virtual processes generate a weak antiferromagnetic next-nearest-neighbour exchange. Finite-size diagnostics are consistent with an effective critical spin-1/2 chain, and 105 accepted positive-region records show no stable internal crossing under the stated rule. At (alpha,beta)=(0.23,0.5), L=40 and q=pi, correction-vector and time-evolution spectra agree; full-momentum maps at three representative points also pass paired time-step convergence gates. These results establish a local-multiplet and effective-chain mechanism, but do not by themselves prove a thermodynamic phase diagram. [Final negative-sector sentence pending Stages A–D.]
Results draft · evidence first

blocks.title: 1 · Local multiplet switch and positive-side effective exchange

blocks.text: The isolated pentamer has S=1/2 for alpha>0, S=3/2 for alpha<0, and an exact degeneracy at alpha=0. This is a local boundary control, not a coupled-chain phase transition. On the positive side, projection at alpha=0.14, 0.23 and 0.33 gives J_eff/beta=0.4396, 0.4318 and 0.4189, establishing antiferromagnetic coupling in the controlled weak-coupling regime.

A second-order construction over 100 positive-alpha points produces an antiferromagnetic next-nearest-neighbour coupling throughout the scan. At the controlled perturbative edge, J2_eff/J1_eff=3.95–5.19%. A three-cell validation changes the fitted spectral-error power to 3.0087–3.0141 when this term is retained, versus 2.0783–2.1861 when it is deleted. This is a quantitative correction, not evidence for a new phase by itself.

The lowest excited doublet has the opposite mirror parity and less than 4.6e-27 weight at q=pi, whereas quartet states carry 84.1–97.6% of the local inelastic weight. This is a local selection rule and must not be relabelled with tetramer-specific quasiparticle names.

The spin gap trends towards zero, correlation exponents lie at 0.95–0.98, and matched-size entanglement calibrations give c=1.0240–1.0331. Across 105 accepted records, L=40/60/80 differences show no stable sign-changing bracket. The supported statement is finite-size no-crossing evidence, not proof of one thermodynamic phase.

At alpha=0.23, beta=0.5, L=40 and q=pi, the accepted11 CV grid and TEBD share a peak at omega=0.05 and differ by 1.04% in shared-window weight. Six full-q runs at three points pass all validators and paired time-step checks; the maximum peak drift is 0.01 J1 and the maximum low-frequency weight drift is 4.32e-5.

blocks.text: Discussion · 核心解释与竞争解释

The principal difference from the reference tetramer chain is unit-cell parity. Four spin-1/2 moments can form singlet or effective integer-spin sectors; five moments leave a half-integer doublet in the positive-coupling local problem. The resulting antiferromagnetic projection, weak induced frustration and momentum filtering are therefore structural consequences of the pentamer rather than a shifted copy of the tetramer phase diagram.

The absence of an accepted positive-region crossing may indicate a common critical regime, but finite sizes and observable sensitivity remain rival explanations. Likewise, a negative-alpha momentum shift may be a crossover or Lifshitz-like line rather than a distinct phase. The final phase map therefore requires non-analytic finite-size evidence from at least two diagnostics.

Provisional title
Odd-unit-cell doublets and effective antiferromagnetism in a 1x5 Heisenberg chain
Abstract

Odd-unit-cell quantum magnets provide a controlled setting in which local multiplet structure and extended-chain dynamics can be separated. We study a 1x5 Heisenberg chain in the non-negative coupling domain, 0<=alpha,beta<=1, using complete single-cell diagonalization, finite-size tensor-network calculations and validated dynamical cross-checks. The five-spin cell retains a low-energy S=1/2 doublet with fixed even mirror parity. Projecting the inter-cell coupling onto this doublet gives a positive effective exchange, J_eff/beta=0.4189--0.4396 at representative points, while two-cell and longer-chain calculations show the leading correction to scale approximately as beta^2. Matched-size finite-size diagnostics are consistent with a c approximately equal to 1 antiferromagnetic chain and the existing positive-region scans contain no stable, acceptance-level internal crossing. At alpha=0.23 and beta=0.5, correction-vector and TEBD spectra agree at q=pi under a documented normalization and coverage protocol. The remaining full-momentum production runs are required before claims about momentum folding and high-energy local branches are finalized. Thus the present evidence establishes an effective-chain mechanism and a bounded no-crossing result, but does not establish a thermodynamic single phase or a new phase boundary.
Introduction

Quantum magnets built from strongly coupled clusters can exhibit low-energy behavior that is not visible from the microscopic bond pattern alone. The parity of the number of spins in a unit cell is especially important: an even cluster may form an internal singlet, whereas an odd cluster necessarily retains an unpaired spin-1/2 degree of freedom. This distinction changes the appropriate question from simply locating a phase boundary to identifying the effective degrees of freedom that survive below the local excitation scale.

Here we investigate the five-spin analogue of a cluster-chain construction in the positive coupling domain. The main technical challenge is to separate robust single-cell symmetry information from finite-size features that can mimic a transition. We therefore combine complete local diagonalization, effective-chain projections, matched-size finite-size diagnostics and independent dynamical checks. The analysis is deliberately restricted to non-negative alpha and beta and does not use the reference Fig.9 sector.

Our goal is not to assume that replacing a 1x4 cell by a 1x5 cell simply translates the reference phase diagram. Instead, we test whether the odd cell produces a surviving doublet, whether the projected inter-cell exchange is antiferromagnetic, and whether the available finite-size data require an additional phase assignment.
Methods

The isolated five-spin cell was diagonalized over the complete 32-dimensional Hilbert space, with total-spin and mirror-parity labels retained. The projected low-energy basis was then used to evaluate the leading inter-cell exchange and its higher-order deviation. Longer chains were treated with finite-size DMRG and entanglement diagnostics at matched sizes. Dynamical response functions were evaluated with correction-vector DMRG and finite-temperature-evolution/TEBD pipelines using Sz=0, open boundaries, explicit t=0 inclusion and raw-spectrum diagnostics. Every production result is required to pass the variance, sector, negative-weight, checksum and independent-validator gates before entering the manuscript evidence set.
Results

The isolated five-spin cell retains an S=1/2 ground-state doublet with even mirror parity throughout the sampled positive-alpha domain. This result is a local symmetry statement: it identifies the low-energy degree of freedom of one cell, but by itself it is not a phase diagram for the infinite chain.

Projecting the inter-cell coupling onto the doublet produces a positive effective exchange. At three representative points, J_eff/beta lies between 0.4189 and 0.4396. The residual between the projected description and the two-cell spectrum scales with an exponent of approximately 1.97--1.99, while matched longer-chain DMRG gives an exponent near 1.95. These results support an antiferromagnetic effective spin-1/2 chain in the controlled weak-coupling regime, with higher local multiplets entering as the coupling is increased.

Finite-size observables are consistent with this effective-chain picture. The extrapolated spin gap approaches zero, correlation exponents lie near 0.95--0.98, and matched-size central-charge calibrations give c=1.0240--1.0331. Independent positive-region scans at L=40, 60 and 80 show no stable sign-changing bracket that would meet the acceptance rule for an internal crossing. The response peaks near alpha approximately 0.17 and 0.30 remain continuous across the tested diagnostics. We therefore report that the present data do not support an additional phase assignment, rather than claiming that the entire thermodynamic quadrant contains only one phase.

At alpha=0.23 and beta=0.5, an accepted eleven-point q=pi correction-vector spectrum brackets the TEBD main peak and covers the prescribed 0--1.5 frequency window under the stated finite-open-chain normalization. The shared-window relative weight difference is about 1.0%, and the two methods locate the peak at the same frequency. This is a production-level Agreement for the stated parameter point, size, momentum and normalization; it is not evidence for all momenta or all couplings.
Discussion

The central result is a mechanism rather than a newly resolved phase boundary. The odd five-spin unit cell leaves a doublet that couples antiferromagnetically between cells, explaining why the low-energy finite-size trends resemble an effective c=1 chain. The local even-parity four-spin excitation remains a distinct high-energy channel in the controlled regime, so low-energy chain physics and local multiplet response should be discussed as coexisting spectral sectors rather than as two phases.

Several boundaries are essential. The c approximately equal to 1 statement is calibrated from finite sizes and should not be presented as an unbiased thermodynamic central-charge extraction. The no-crossing statement is limited to the sampled positive-region sizes and observables. The q=pi Agreement is limited to alpha=0.23, beta=0.5, L=40 and the documented normalization. Full-momentum production data at the three representative points are still needed to decide whether the predicted momentum folding and high-energy branch assignment survive the dt/dt2 convergence gates.
Conclusion

The current evidence supports a five-spin odd-unit-cell mechanism: a surviving S=1/2 doublet generates an effective antiferromagnetic chain, while local multiplet channels remain at higher energy. Finite-size scans do not require an internal positive-region crossing, and one q=pi dynamical instance passes an independent CV--TEBD Agreement gate. These findings justify writing the local mechanism, finite-size evidence and bounded dynamical result now. The final phase-level and full-momentum claims must remain provisional until the remaining six-cell full-q campaign and its dt/dt2 acceptance analysis are complete.

blocks.text: 参考论文的 Fig. 6–8 使用 Krylov-space correction vector DMRG，而旧五聚体 pilot 使用实时 TEBD。为避免在大系统上放大方法错误，本轮先在 $L=10$、固定 $S^z=0$ 的 252 维扇区计算完整精确谱，再用同一 Hamiltonian、动量算符、展宽和频率网格验证 ITensor 修正向量实现。

blocks.text: 本地控制器和服务器分工

items: phase policy、observations、state、report 和 crossing 决策只在 Windows 本地运行；已加入 fcntl 兼容入口并通过 scaffold/init/check/ingest/inspect smoke。
服务器只接收 parameter-scan compute entrypoint 和 run spec；不上传控制器、state 或认证信息。首段已按用户确认上传，远端 PID=3436382。
每个 phase cell 内部运行 center/domain 两个独立初态，回传一个带 value/error 的 manifest；回传前不接受调度器状态作为科学成功。
首段粗扫共 30 个 cell（3 个 beta × 5 个 alpha × 2 个初始尺寸）；30 个 action spec 已逐一落盘并与 controller 授权 ID 对齐。
positive_phase_guard 会把‘无显著 crossing’与‘数据不足’分开；前者可作为正区无相界证据，后者必须继续计算。
upload_phase_bundle.ps1 需要显式‘确认首段’，并在断线重试时按远端 SHA-256 跳过已完成文件；首个失败 cell 已移入 cells_failed/cell-0001_initial_failure 作为审计记录。
domain 初态采用固定种子 randomMPS(sites,state,4)，配合 1e-6/1e-7/1e-8 小噪声，保持 QN 扇区和可复现性；这修复了 alpha=0,beta=0.1 的高能局域态陷阱。

blocks.text: Skill 改进建议

items: 上传脚本应区分‘SSH 连接超时’与‘远端 SHA-256 不匹配’，对前者做有限指数重试，不要直接报 hash mismatch。
phase cell runner 应默认提供固定种子的随机 QN-MPS 或参数延续初态；确定性 domain 产品态可能停在高能局域本征态。
alpha=0 存在简并基态时，双初态 observable 半差可能是物理简并而非数值误差；应标记 degeneracy 并禁止用该点单独命名相界。
Windows 报告工具应显式使用 UTF-8，避免系统 GBK 导致中文 JSON/脚本渲染失败。
